sources.title: Codex Leningradensis (B19a)
sources.author: Samuel ben Jacob (Scribe / Masorete)
sources.publisher: National Library of Russia, St. Petersburg
sources.edition: Facsimile Edition by D.N. Freedman et al. (Eerdmans, 1998); basis for BHS & BHQ

provenance.methodology: High-resolution multi-spectral photographic autopsy and diplomatic transcription

sources.notes: Oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible based on Aaron ben Moses ben Asher Masorah.

sources.title: Aleppo Codex (Keter Aram Tzova)
sources.author: Shlomo ben Buya'a (Scribe), Aaron ben Moses ben Asher (Masorete)
sources.edition: The Aleppo Codex, ed. M.H. Goshen-Gottstein (Hebrew University, 1976)
sources.identifier: Israel Museum Shrine of the Book
sources.repository: Shrine of the Book, Israel Museum, Jerusalem

provenance.methodology: Scholarly autopsy by Goshen-Gottstein, Breuer, Ofer

sources.notes: Endorsed by Maimonides (Hilkhot Sefer Torah 8:4) as authoritative model for Torah scrolls; missing parts lost in 1947.

sources.title: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a)
sources.author: Judean / Qumran Scribes
sources.publisher: Israel Exploration Society / Shrine of the Book
sources.edition: Discoveries in the Judaean Desert (DJD) / Ulrich & Flint edition (2010)

provenance.methodology: Radiocarbon dating and full digital imaging and orthographic analysis

sources.notes: Contains complete text of Isaiah demonstrating over 95% textual agreement with MT over a 1,100-year transmission span, with orthographic plene spelling variations.

sources.title: Qumran Sectarian Halakhic Letter (4QMMT / 4Q394-399)
sources.author: Teacher of Righteousness / Qumran Leadership
sources.edition: DJD X: Qumran Cave 4.V: Miqsat Ma'ase ha-Torah, ed. E. Qimron & J. Strugnell (1994)

provenance.methodology: Composite manuscript reconstruction from six fragmentary copies

sources.notes: Essential evidence for Second Temple halakhic disputes on temple purity, calendar, and sacrificial law matching Sadducean halakhot mentioned in Mishnah Yadayim 4:6-7.

sources.title: Septuaginta: Vetus Testamentum Graecum (Critical Edition)
sources.author: Alexandrian Jewish Translators / Alfred Rahlfs & Robert Hanhart (eds.)
sources.edition: Septuaginta: Id est Vetus Testamentum graece iuxta LXX interpretes, ed. Rahlfs-Hanhart (2006)

provenance.methodology: Textual-critical reconstruction based on oldest uncial and papyrus witnesses

sources.notes: Primary Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible produced by Hellenistic Jews; demonstrates differences in Vorlage (e.g. shorter Jeremiah, differing chronology in Kings).

sources.title: Samaritan Pentateuch (Critical Edition)
sources.author: Samaritan Scribes / August von Gall & Abraham Tal (eds.)
sources.edition: The Samaritan Pentateuch: Edited by Abraham Tal and Moshe Florentin (2010)

provenance.methodology: Collation of ancient Samaritan Pentateuch manuscripts and DSS parallels

sources.notes: Contains ~6,000 variants from MT, including ~1,900 shared with LXX and explicit Mount Gerizim sectarian additions in the Decalogue.

sources.title: Tel Dan Stele ('House of David' Inscription)
sources.author: Aramaean King (likely Hazael)
sources.edition: Biran & Naveh (1993, 1995) in IEJ 43, pp. 81-98; IEJ 45, pp. 1-18

provenance.methodology: Archaeological excavation in situ and epigraphical analysis

sources.notes: Extra-biblical epigraphic confirmation of the Davidic dynasty (Bytdwd / House of David) and the King of Israel in the 9th century BCE.

sources.title: Ketef Hinnom Silver Amulets (KH1 & KH2)
sources.author: Judahite Silversmith / Priestly Scribe
sources.edition: Barkay et al. (2004) in BASOR 334, pp. 41-71

provenance.methodology: High-resolution digital imaging and palaeographic analysis

sources.notes: Oldest surviving citations of biblical texts: the Priestly Blessing (Birkat Kohanim, Numbers 6:24-26) and Deuteronomy 7:9 dating before the Babylonian Exile.

sources.title: Philo of Alexandria: Complete Works
sources.author: Philo Judaeus (Philo of Alexandria)
sources.edition: Philo in Ten Volumes, trans. F.H. Colson & G.H. Whitaker (LCL, 1929–1962)
sources.repository: Bibliotheque Nationale de France / Vatican Library

provenance.methodology: Critical Greek collation and translation

sources.notes: Essential primary witness for Hellenistic Jewish allegorical exegesis, Middle Platonic synthesis, and the concept of the divine Logos.

sources.title: Flavius Josephus: Jewish Antiquities & The Jewish War
sources.author: Yosef ben Matityahu (Flavius Josephus)
sources.language: Koine Greek (originally drafted in Aramaic for War)
sources.edition: Josephus: The Jewish War & Jewish Antiquities, ed. H.St.J. Thackeray, Ralph Marcus, Louis H. Feldman

provenance.methodology: Critical apparatus collation of Benedictus Niese edition

sources.notes: Indispensable historical chronicle of the Second Temple period, the Great Jewish Revolt, sectarian philosophies (Pharisees, Sadducees, Essenes), and Testimonium Flavianum.

sources.title: The Mishnah (MS Kaufmann A 50 & Critical Editions)
sources.author: Rabbi Yehudah Ha-Nasi (Redactor)
sources.edition: Shishah Sidrei Mishnah, ed. Chanoch Albeck & Hanoch Yalon (Jerusalem, 1952–1958); MS Kaufmann A 50 (facsimile ed. G. Beer 1929)
sources.identifier: Library of Hungarian Academy of Sciences MS A 50
sources.repository: Budapest, Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences

provenance.methodology: Linguistic and philological critical comparison against Parma and Cambridge MSS

sources.notes: Foundational code of the Oral Torah organized into Six Orders (Zeraim, Moed, Nashim, Nezikin, Kodashim, Tohorot), containing 63 tractates.

sources.title: The Tosefta (Lieberman Critical Edition)
sources.author: Rabbi Hiyya & Rabbi Oshaya (Traditional Redactors)
sources.edition: The Tosefta According to Codex Vienna with Variants, ed. Saul Lieberman (New York, 1955–1988)
sources.repository: Austrian National Library, Vienna (Codex Vienna Hebr. 20)

provenance.methodology: Rigorous critical collation with Tosefta Ki-Fshutah multi-volume commentary

sources.notes: Supplement and parallel corpus to the Mishnah, preserving alternative baraitot and earlier legal traditions.

sources.title: Babylonian Talmud (Talmud Bavli) — Vilna Romm Edition & Munich 95
sources.author: Rav Ashi, Ravina, and the Savoraim
sources.publisher: Romm Publishing House, Vilna / Bayerische Staatsbibliothek
sources.edition: Vilna Shas (1880–1886); Munich Codex Hebraicus 95 (1342 CE complete MS)

provenance.methodology: Critical collation by Dikdukei Soferim (R.N.N. Rabbinovicz, 1867–1897)

sources.notes: The supreme authoritative text of rabbinic Judaism, establishing Halakha, Aggadah, theology, and legal dialectic across 37 tractates.

sources.title: Jerusalem Talmud (Talmud Yerushalmi / Palestinian Talmud)
sources.author: Amoraim of the Land of Israel (Rabbi Yochanan et al.)
sources.region: Tiberias, Sepphoris, Caesarea, Land of Israel
sources.publisher: Daniel Bomberg, Venice (1523) / Academy of the Hebrew Language
sources.edition: Codex Leiden Scal. 3 (Sole surviving complete MS, copied 1289 CE)

provenance.methodology: Academy of the Hebrew Language critical edition and transcription (2001)

sources.notes: Redacted under Roman-Byzantine pressure prior to the Babylonian Talmud; contains extensive coverage of the agricultural laws of Zeraim.

sources.title: Mekhilta de-Rabbi Ishmael (Horovitz-Rabin Critical Edition)
sources.author: Tannaim of the School of Rabbi Ishmael
sources.edition: Mechiltha d'Rabbi Ismael, ed. H.S. Horovitz & I.A. Rabin (Frankfurt 1931 / Jerusalem 1970)
sources.manuscript_reference: MS Oxford Heb. c. 18, MS Munich 117

provenance.methodology: Textual collation of European and Cairo Genizah manuscripts

sources.notes: Classical tannaitic legal exegesis on the Book of Exodus (chapters 12 to 35).

sources.title: Bereshit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah — Theodor-Albeck Edition)
sources.author: Amoraim of the Land of Israel
sources.edition: Bereschit Rabba mit kritischem Apparat, ed. J. Theodor & Ch. Albeck (Berlin 1903–1936)
sources.manuscript_reference: MS Vatican Heb. 30 (oldest complete midrashic MS)

provenance.methodology: Monumental critical apparatus collating MS Vatican 30, 60, and Genizah remnants

sources.notes: The primary classic aggadic midrash on Genesis, rich in theology, eschatology, and polemics against Roman paganism and early Christianity.

sources.title: Saadia Gaon: Kitab al-Amanat wal-I'tiqadat (Book of Beliefs and Opinions)
sources.author: Saadia ben Joseph Gaon
sources.language: Judeo-Arabic (translated into Hebrew by Judah ibn Tibbon as Sefer Ha-Emunot ve-ha-Deot)
sources.publisher: Yale University Press (Rosenblatt trans.) / Landauer Arabic edition
sources.edition: The Book of Beliefs and Opinions, trans. Samuel Rosenblatt (Yale Judaica Series, 1948); ed. Yosef Qafih (Jerusalem 1970)
sources.repository: Bodleian Library / National Library of Russia

provenance.methodology: Critical reading of Judeo-Arabic text against Arabic Kalam and Mu'tazilite philosophy

sources.notes: First systematic philosophical defense of rabbinic Judaism, refuting Christian Trinity, Islamic abrogation (naskh) of Torah, and Karaite anti-rabbinism.

sources.title: Rashi's Commentary on the Tanakh and Talmud
sources.author: Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki (Rashi)
sources.language: Medieval Rabbinic Hebrew with Old French glosses (La'azim)
sources.edition: Perushei Rashi al Ha-Torah, ed. Chaim Dov Chavel (Jerusalem, 1982); Vilna Talmud Rashi text
sources.repository: Multiple European and Israeli National Library MSS

provenance.methodology: Manuscript collation with critical focus on peshat vs derash

sources.notes: The universally authoritative commentary combining literal contextual exegesis (peshat) with selected midrashic insights; essential for understanding traditional Jewish interpretation of Isaiah 53 and messianic passages.

sources.title: Maimonides: Mishneh Torah (Yad Ha-Chazaqah)
sources.author: Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon (Maimonides / Rambam)
sources.edition: Mishneh Torah Frankel Edition (Jerusalem 1975–2001); ed. Yosef Qafih; Oxford Bodleian Huntington 80 (with Rambam's autograph signature)
sources.manuscript_reference: MS Hunt. 80 (signed 'Huga be-sifri' / corrected from my book by Moses son of Maimon)

provenance.methodology: Autograph and authorized manuscript verification

sources.notes: The 14-volume comprehensive code of all Jewish law; includes Sefer Ha-Madda (foundational theological dogmas, monotheism, prophecy) and Hilkhot Melakhim (chapters 11-12 on the King Messiah, messianic criteria, and historical analysis of Jesus and Muhammad).

sources.title: Maimonides: Guide of the Perplexed (Dalalat al-Ha'irin)
sources.author: Rabbi Moshe ben Maimon (Maimonides / Rambam)
sources.edition: The Guide of the Perplexed, trans. Shlomo Pines (Chicago, 1963, 2 vols.); Arabic text ed. Salomon Munk
sources.repository: Bibliotheque Nationale de France / Oxford Bodleian

provenance.methodology: Philosophical-philological translation from original Judeo-Arabic text with Leo Strauss introductory essay

sources.notes: Masterwork of medieval Jewish rationalist philosophy synthesizing Aristotelianism and biblical revelation, negative theology, divine incorporeality, prophecy, and the problem of evil.

sources.title: Nachmanides: Commentary on the Torah & Barcelona Disputation
sources.author: Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman (Nachmanides / Ramban)
sources.region: Girona, Catalonia / Acre, Land of Israel
sources.edition: Perushei Ha-Torah le-Rabbenu Moshe ben Nachman, ed. Chaim Dov Chavel (Jerusalem 1959–1960); Kitvei Ha-Ramban (Vikuach Ha-Ramban)

provenance.methodology: Critical apparatus and historical comparison with Latin conciliar records of the 1263 Barcelona Disputation

sources.notes: Integrates peshat, kabbalistic allusions (sod), psychological insight, and historical polemics defending Judaism against Christian convert Pablo Christiani before King James I of Aragon.

sources.title: Judah Halevi: Kitab al-Radd wa-al-Dalil fi al-Din al-Dhalil (The Kuzari)
sources.author: Rabbi Judah Halevi
sources.language: Judeo-Arabic (Hebrew trans. by Judah ibn Tibbon)
sources.region: Cordoba / Toledo, Islamic and Christian Spain
sources.edition: The Kuzari, trans. Hartwig Hirschfeld (1905); ed. David H. Baneth & Haggai Ben-Shammai (Magnes, 1977)

provenance.methodology: Judeo-Arabic critical edition of the dialogue with the Khazar King

sources.notes: Philosophical dialogue arguing for the superiority of historical national revelation (the Sinai covenant witnessed by 600,000 men) over philosophical rationalism and sectarian claims.

sources.title: Shulchan Aruch with Mappah (Code of Jewish Law)
sources.author: Rabbi Joseph Karo (Sephardic) & Rabbi Moses Isserles (Rema, Ashkenazic)
sources.publisher: Juan di Gara (Venice 1565) / Isaac ben Aaron Prostitz (Cracow 1578)
sources.edition: Standard Vilna Edition with Major Commentaries (Taz, Shach, Magen Avraham)
sources.manuscript_reference: Early printings and rabbinic responsa collations

provenance.methodology: Comparative halakhic synthesis of Rif, Rambam, and Rosh with Ashkenazi custom (Minhag)

sources.notes: The authoritative normative code of Halakha comprising four sections: Orach Chayim (prayer/festivals), Yoreh De'ah (dietary/purity), Even Ha-Ezer (marriage/divorce), and Choshen Mishpat (jurisprudence/civil law).

sources.title: Rabbi Moshe Feinstein: Igrot Moshe (Responsa Collection)
sources.author: Rabbi Moshe Feinstein
sources.edition: Igrot Moshe, 8 volumes (New York 1959–1996)

provenance.methodology: Halakhic legal analysis of modern medical ethics, technology, Kashrut, and interfaith boundaries

sources.notes: Widely recognized halakhic decisor (Posek Ha-Dor) of 20th-century American and global Orthodoxy.

sources.title: Rabbi Joseph B. Soloveitchik: Halakhic Man & The Lonely Man of Faith
sources.author: Rabbi Joseph B. Soloveitchik (The Rav)
sources.edition: Halakhic Man, trans. Lawrence Kaplan (JPS, 1983); The Lonely Man of Faith (Doubleday, 1965)
sources.manuscript_reference: Original essays in Talpiot and Tradition

provenance.methodology: Philosophical phenomenology of halakhic consciousness integrating Neo-Kantianism and Brisker Talmudic analysis

sources.notes: Intellectual architect of Modern Orthodoxy articulating the creative dignity of the Halakhic personality engaging modern reality.

sources.title: Central Conference of American Rabbis (CCAR) Platforms (1885, 1937, 1976, 1999)
sources.author: Central Conference of American Rabbis (Reform Leadership)
sources.edition: A Statement of Principles for Reform Judaism (1999 San Francisco Platform); The Pittsburgh Platform (1885)

provenance.methodology: Historical-critical evolution from radical 1885 Pittsburgh rejection of ritual dietary laws to 1999 reclaimed traditionalism

sources.notes: Official theological platforms tracing the trajectory of Reform Judaism regarding God, Torah, Mitzvot, Land of Israel, and social justice (Tikkun Olam).

sources.title: Committee on Jewish Law and Standards (CJLS) Responsa Collection
sources.author: Rabbinical Assembly / CJLS Rabbis (Conservative Movement)
sources.edition: Proceedings of the Committee on Jewish Law and Standards (multiple volumes 1927–2020)

provenance.methodology: Application of historical-critical halakhic jurisprudence balancing tradition and change

sources.notes: Authoritative halakhic rulings of Conservative Judaism regarding Shabbat driving, women's rabbinic ordination, Kashrut standards, and marriage equality.

sources.title: Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd Revised Edition)
sources.author: Emanuel Tov (Professor of Bible, Hebrew University of Jerusalem)
sources.edition: 3rd Revised and Expanded Edition (2012)

provenance.methodology: Definitive handbook of Hebrew textual criticism synthesizing MT, DSS, LXX, SP, and Targumim

sources.notes: The universally acclaimed standard academic manual on the scribal transmission, textual diversity, and reconstruction of the Hebrew Bible.

sources.title: Reclaiming the Dead Sea Scrolls: Their True Meaning for Judaism and Christianity
sources.author: Lawrence H. Schiffman (New York University)
sources.edition: Anchor Bible Reference Library / JPS Edition (1994)

provenance.methodology: Analysis of Qumran sectarian legal texts (4QMMT, Temple Scroll, Damascus Document) in relation to rabbinic halakha

sources.notes: Establishes that the Dead Sea Scrolls reflect Jewish sectarian legal controversies and Sadducean-type halakha rather than proto-Christian beliefs.

sources.title: Judaism: Practice and Belief 63 BCE–66 CE
sources.author: E.P. Sanders (Duke University)
sources.edition: First Edition (1992)

provenance.methodology: Pioneering historiography establishing 'Common Judaism' (temple, priesthood, festivals, Torah) shared by non-sectarian ordinary Jews

sources.notes: Dismantles 19th-century caricatures of late Second Temple Judaism as a dry legalistic religion; established modern scholarly consensus on covenantal nomism.

sources.title: From the Maccabees to the Mishnah (3rd Edition)
sources.author: Shaye J.D. Cohen (Harvard University)
sources.edition: 3rd Edition (2014)
sources.manuscript_reference: Synthesis of Second Temple & Rabbinic evolution

provenance.methodology: Critical analysis of Jewish identity boundaries, canon formation, and sectarian development

sources.notes: Essential textbook analyzing how ancient Judean national religion transformed into rabbinic Judaism following the destruction of the Temple.

sources.title: Isaac of Troki: Hizzuk Emunah (Faith Strengthened)
sources.author: Isaac ben Abraham of Troki (Karaite Scholar)
sources.publisher: Johann Christoph Wagenseil (Tela Ignea Satanae, 1681) / Moses Mocatta trans. (London 1851)
sources.edition: Faith Strengthened, trans. Moses Mocatta (Hermon Press reprint 1970); ed. David Berger

provenance.methodology: Systematic chapter-by-chapter Jewish refutation of Christian messianic claims, New Testament contradictions, and proof-texts

sources.notes: The most famous Jewish anti-Christian polemical work; praised even by Voltaire for its formidable textual and rational critiques.

sources.title: Ibn Hazm of Cordoba: Al-Fasl fi al-Milal wal-Ahwa' wan-Nihal (The Decisive Word on Sects)
sources.author: Abu Muhammad Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Hazm
sources.publisher: Maktabat al-Khanji, Cairo (1903) / Dar al-Jil, Beirut (1996)
sources.edition: Al-Fasl, ed. Muhammad Ibrahim Nasr & Abd al-Rahman Umayrah (Beirut 1996, 5 vols.)

provenance.methodology: Radical literalist critique arguing for total textual corruption (Tahrif al-Nass) of the Hebrew Bible and Christian Gospels

sources.notes: Foundational Islamic polemical work formulating the doctrine of Tahrif al-Nass; argued that Ezra fabricated the Torah after the Babylonian exile.

sources.title: A Hebrew and English Lexicon of the Old Testament (Brown-Driver-Briggs / BDB)
sources.author: Francis Brown, S. R. Driver, and Charles A. Briggs
sources.region: Oxford, United Kingdom / Boston, United States
sources.edition: Oxford Clarendon Press 1906 / Hendrickson Publishers reprint
sources.manuscript_reference: Standard biblical Hebrew lexicon based on Wilhelm Gesenius

provenance.methodology: Exhaustive comparative Semitic etymology, root-based morphology, and biblical concordance cross-referencing

sources.notes: The definitive classical reference lexicon for Biblical Hebrew and Biblical Aramaic, organized by triliteral roots with comparative Semitic cognates.

sources.title: The Bible in Aramaic (Targum Onkelos and Targum Jonathan)
sources.author: Onkelos / Jonathan ben Uzziel (Traditional Attributions); Alexander Sperber (Editor)
sources.language: Jewish Palestinian Aramaic / Jewish Babylonian Aramaic
sources.edition: The Bible in Aramaic: Based on Old Manuscripts and Printed Texts (5 vols., 1959–1973)
sources.manuscript_reference: MS British Museum Or. 2210 / Vatican Neofiti 1

provenance.methodology: Diplomatic edition of vocalized Yemenite and Western Aramaic manuscripts

sources.notes: Standard academic critical edition of the authorized Aramaic Targumim to the Torah and Prophets.

sources.title: The Traditional Jewish Daily and Festival Prayer Book (Siddur / Mahzor)
sources.author: Traditional Sages (Anshei Knesset Ha-Gedolah, Rav Amram Gaon, Saadia Gaon)
sources.date: c. 9th–12th century CE compilation (grounded in Tannaitic/Amoraic liturgy)
sources.approximate_date: Geonic stabilization (c. 870 CE Seder Rav Amram Gaon)
sources.region: Babylonia, Land of Israel, Europe, Middle East
sources.publisher: Koren Publishers Jerusalem / Mossad Harav Kook
sources.edition: Siddur Koren Sacks (2009) / Seder Rav Amram Gaon (Goldschmidt ed., Mossad Harav Kook 1971)
sources.repository: Bodleian Library, Oxford (MS Oppenheim 59) / Jewish Theological Seminary
sources.manuscript_reference: Seder Rav Amram Gaon MS Oxford 1095

provenance.methodology: Comparative liturgical collation of Geonic manuscripts and classical Ashkenazi/Sephardi rites

sources.notes: Preserves the canonical post-70 liturgical replacement of sacrificial rites via Shemoneh Esreh, Musaf, and Avodah recitations.

sources.title: Jami' al-Bayan 'an Ta'wil Ay al-Qur'an (Tafsir al-Tabari)
sources.author: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari
sources.edition: Critical edition edited by Ahmad and Mahmud Shakir (16 vols., 1954–1968)
sources.identifier: National Library of Egypt (Dar al-Kutub) MS 119 Tafsir
sources.repository: Dar al-Kutub, Cairo / Suleymaniye Library, Istanbul

provenance.methodology: Classical Arabic philological and riwayah chain-of-transmission exegesis

sources.notes: Paramount foundational classical commentary establishing Tahrif al-Ma'na (distortion of meaning/exegesis) rather than physical textual erasure on Surah 2:75 and 3:78.

sources.title: Kitab al-Anwar wal-Maraqib (The Book of Lights and Watchtowers)
sources.author: Ya'qub al-Qirqisani
sources.publisher: Alexander Kohut Memorial Foundation, New York
sources.edition: Critical edition edited by Leon Nemoy (5 vols., 1939–1943)
sources.repository: National Library of Russia, St. Petersburg (Firkovich Collection)

provenance.methodology: Critical collation of Judeo-Arabic manuscripts from the Firkovich collections

sources.notes: Comprehensive encyclopedic Karaite legal and historical code rejecting Rabbinic Oral Law and detailing Second Temple sects.

sources.title: Likkutei Amarim (Tanya)
sources.author: Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi (The Alter Rebbe)
sources.edition: Bi-lingual Hebrew-English Edition with Annotations and Sources (1984/2002)
sources.repository: Library of Agudas Chasidei Chabad, 770 Eastern Parkway, Brooklyn, NY

provenance.methodology: Systematic Kabbalistic and Hasidic psychological theological exposition

sources.notes: The foundational philosophical and mystical text of Chabad-Lubavitch Hasidism, articulating panentheism (Ein Od Milvado) and the struggle between animal and divine souls.

sources.title: Sefer ha-Zohar (The Zohar: Pritzker Edition)
sources.author: Attributed to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai; composed/redacted by Moses de Leon (Castile, 13th c.)
sources.edition: The Zohar: Pritzker Edition, Translation and Commentary by Daniel C. Matt (12 vols., 2004–2017)
sources.repository: Bibliothèque nationale de France (BnF héb. 781) / Cambridge University Library
sources.manuscript_reference: MS BnF hébreu 781 / MS Cambridge Add. 1023

provenance.methodology: Critical manuscript recension, Aramaic philology, and historical-mystical contextual analysis

sources.notes: The central foundational work of Jewish mystical thought (Kabbalah), framing the Sefirot, divine emanations, and the theurgic cosmic role of mitzvot.

sources.title: Judaism as a Civilization: Toward a Reconstruction of American-Jewish Life
sources.author: Mordecai M. Kaplan
sources.publisher: Macmillan Company (1934) / Jewish Publication Society reprint (2010)
sources.edition: 75th Anniversary Edition with Introduction by Arnold M. Eisen (JPS, 2010)
sources.repository: Library of the Jewish Theological Seminary, New York

provenance.methodology: Sociological, naturalistic philosophical analysis of Jewish identity and religious evolution

sources.notes: Founding manifesto of Reconstructionist Judaism defining Judaism as an evolving religious civilization rather than a static supernatural revelation.
